To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the information-theoretic approach is a viable alternative to linguistic approaches to text readability.

(i) the classifier based on information-theory features outperforms the linguistic classifier; (ii) the best results are obtained with a classifier based on a combination of information-theoretic and linguistic features; (iii) the best results for both classifiers are obtained with a feature selection technique based on the information gain; and (iv) the best results of the linguistic classifier are obtained when we combine the features of all linguistic levels.

(1) information-theoretic measures are useful for text readability classification; (2) the combination of information-theoretic and linguistic features outperform both approaches; and (3) information-theoretically-based classifiers perform as well as linguistic-based ones, and in some cases, even better, when the linguistic features are used in combination.

we show that it is possible to develop an automatic readability classification of text based on information-theoretical measures.
the use of information-theoretic measures is a promising approach to the classification of text readability, and can provide valuable insights to the linguistic analysis of readability.
the linguistic approach to readability is a good starting point for developing a readability classifier.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the information-theoretic approach to readability can be used in combination with linguistic ones to improve the accuracy of readability classifiers.

information-theoretics features can be used to automatically identify the readability of texts and can be used as an additional feature for other tasks that rely on text readability, e.g., text simplification, summarization and text classification.
